19fa8e4dfc650a5bcfcb504a8f38920f6061c863.summary: Vendor report from the Aqua Nautilus team on the Kinsing campaign, active since 2019. Kinsing exploits vulnerable or misconfigured applications and exposed Docker APIs, runs a Monero cryptominer often hidden by a rootkit, and keeps control through the Kinsing malware. The report covers 75 targeted applications, the scripts and binaries used, a comparison of malware samples with CyberArk's 2021 analysis, and a MITRE ATT&CK mapping. Its remarks on Russian or Chinese origins are speculation it hedges.

hedges: The report says infrastructure choices may suggest a connection to Russian-speaking countries, which could imply Russian origins for the threat actor.
The report did not find a single answer on whether Kinsing is one threat actor, a malware name, or leaked source code.
The report says the C2 website change might be a defense evasion strategy, or that the website may have been compromised.
The report says there is no definitive proof that the threat actor actively uses masscan.
The report says it is not sure the operator owns the C2 website domain.
The report says the list of targeted applications is not exhaustive and some remain unclassified.
The report says the exact reason for the two script types is known only to the threat actor.
The report says it may have failed to understand the full scope of the mining operation.

19b2258d841699869a494c3752d0f7ec9b1ba3d2.summary: Avast's Threat Intelligence Team (21 February 2018) describes Tempting Cedar Spyware, an APT spread through fake Facebook profiles that lured victims to a fake Kik Messenger app. The Android spyware was designed to steal contacts, call logs, SMS and photos, track location, record surrounding audio, and persist after reboot, with a C&C console giving live tracking. Most victims were in the Middle East, mainly Israel, and the campaign ran from as far back as 2015. The report believes the operators are Lebanese but says it cannot be 100% sure. Avast detects it as Android:SpyAgent-YP.
